auth.lead: Short, positive daily guidance and a shared log for the whole family.
auth.tagline: Train your puppy, a little every day

cold.message: Raised kennel, dry straw and shelter from the wind.
cold.title: Cold

firstWeekVet.message: Checkup, health record and microchip. Ask about the vaccination schedule, year-round deworming and leishmaniasis prevention, which is common in the area. Talk to your vet.
firstWeekVet.title: First week: vet

grassAwns.message: Check ears, paws and nose after every walk.
grassAwns.title: Grass awns

livestockAndHens.message: Don't let her off leash nearby until she has mastered "come" and "leave it".
livestockAndHens.title: Livestock and hens

pineProcessionary.message: Keep her away from pine trees and lines of caterpillars. If she touches or bites them: veterinary emergency.
pineProcessionary.title: Pine processionary caterpillars

poisonsAndChemicals.message: Keep poisons, fertilizers, diesel and workshop products out of reach.
poisonsAndChemicals.title: Poisons and chemicals

ticksAndHeat.message: Always shade and fresh water. Parasite protection: talk to your vet.
ticksAndHeat.title: Ticks and heat

unknownDogsUntilVaccinated.message: No contact with unknown dogs until she has completed the vaccination schedule your vet recommends.
unknownDogsUntilVaccinated.title: Unknown dogs

week1.readyWhen: Turns her head when she hears her name

week2.how: Reward over the head; same potty spot every time
week2.readyWhen: Sits for the hand signal, with no treat in the hand

week3.how: Crouch down, happy voice, play between two people

week4.how: Leash indoors; "ouch" and stop the game
week4.readyWhen: Walks a few yards on leash

week5.how: Treat from nose to floor; closed fist
week5.readyWhen: Moves away from a closed hand

bowls.label: Heavy food and water bowls that do not tip over

breederFood.label: The same puppy food the breeder uses, for the first days

cleaning.hint: Enzymatic cleaner breaks down the smell of pee and poop, so she doesn't go back to the same spot. Don't use bleach or ammonia: they smell like urine. The bags are for picking up poop.
cleaning.label: Enzymatic cleaner and bags for accidents

collarAndLeash.label: A soft collar with an ID tag and a light leash

familyRules.label: Family rules: the same word for each cue, who feeds her and where she sleeps

kennel.label: A kennel raised off the ground, sheltered from wind and rain, with dry bedding

litterBlanket.label: A blanket with the smell of her litter (ask the breeder)

safeArea.label: A safe area: close off the workshop, tools, chemicals and cables

toys.label: Chew toys and a tug toy, as an alternative to biting

vetVisit.label: A vet appointment for the first week

principles.calmPlay: Play is fine, but chasing over and over (balls, sticks) shouldn't be the center of her day; balance it with exploring and calm.
principles.endWell: Always end on a good note.
principles.foodAndSleep: She eats 3 times a day until 4–6 months and sleeps 16–18 hours.
principles.lowerDifficulty: If something isn't working, make it easier.
principles.noFenceWatching: Watching the fence or the road isn't her job: don't let her spend hours on guard.
principles.restAfterActivity: After activity comes rest: go out, train, eat, sleep.
principles.sameWords: Everyone uses the same words: {{name}}, come, sit, down, stay, joga, leave it, off, heel, fetch, good.
principles.shortSessions: Sessions of 3 to 5 minutes, several times a day.
principles.smallRewards: Pea-sized treats taken from her daily food. A special treat (boiled chicken) only for "come".
principles.sniffing: Let her use her nose: hide a few treats in the grass and let her find them.

howTo.levelUp: She stays calm 4 times out of 5: brush a little longer and add her chest, legs and tail.
howTo.mistakes: Brushing against the coat, pulling on knots, and brushing for a long time when she is excited.
howTo.setup: A soft brush and a few treats. A quiet moment in the evening, before bed.
howTo.step1: Let her sniff the brush and give her a treat.
howTo.step2: Make one short stroke along her back, say “good” and give a treat.
howTo.step3: Add strokes one at a time along her back and sides, in the direction of the coat.
howTo.step4: Stop after a minute or two, while she is calm, and finish with a gentle game.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she bites the brush or wriggles, give her a chew toy to hold, go back to one stroke and reward more often.

howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed 4 times out of 5: hold a little longer, or bring a towel or a brush she can see and sniff first.
howTo.mistakes: Holding her down while she struggles, handling her only when something has to be done, and long sessions.
howTo.setup: A calm moment, ideally after a nap or a walk. Small treats at hand and a soft surface where she can sit or lie down.
howTo.step1: Touch a paw for one second, say “good” and give a treat. Do the same with an ear.
howTo.step2: Little by little, hold the paw a bit longer, gently spread the toes and look inside the ear.
howTo.step3: Reward every touch, even the short ones, and stop before she tries to pull away.
howTo.step4: Practice what the vet will do: lift her lips to see her teeth, touch her belly and her tail.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she pulls away or mouths your hand, you went too fast: go back to a shorter touch she accepts and reward more often.

howTo.levelUp: She goes in and settles 4 nights out of 5: keep the routine short and at the same time every night.
howTo.mistakes: Using the kennel as a punishment, long goodbyes, changing the routine every night, and playing with her when she cries.
howTo.setup: A raised kennel sheltered from wind and rain, with dry bedding, her blanket and a chew toy. Practice during the day before using it at night.
howTo.step1: During the day, toss treats into the kennel and let her go in and out freely; say “good” when she goes in.
howTo.step2: Give her a meal or a chew toy inside, so the kennel means good things.
howTo.step3: At bedtime, follow the same calm routine every night: potty, a short quiet moment, then to the kennel with her blanket.
howTo.step4: Say goodnight calmly and leave, without a long goodbye.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she cries, check calmly that she does not need to go potty and that she is warm and dry, then leave again without playing; on cold nights follow the cold alert.

howTo.levelUp: She stays relaxed and curious 4 times out of 5: get a little closer, or make it a little louder or longer, one change at a time.
howTo.mistakes: Forcing her to face what scares her, too many new things in one day, and missing the signs of fear.
howTo.setup: Pick one new experience from the checklist. Have tasty treats ready and choose a distance at which she stays relaxed: loose body, wagging tail, curious.
howTo.step1: Let her watch the new thing from that distance; every time she looks at it calmly, say “good” and give a treat.
howTo.step2: Let her choose to get closer; never carry or pull her toward it.
howTo.step3: If she sniffs or explores on her own, praise her quietly and keep the treats coming.
howTo.step4: Stop after a few minutes, while she is still relaxed, and go somewhere calm.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she freezes, tucks her tail, hides or will not take treats, she is too close: move away calmly until she relaxes, and next time start farther away.

afternoonRest.instructions: Long nap. Potty break when she wakes up.
afternoonRest.title: Rest

bedtime.instructions: Into the kennel with her blanket and a chew toy. Same routine every night and a calm goodbye.
bedtime.title: Bedtime in the kennel

breakfast.instructions: "Sit" before the bowl goes down. If she doesn't sit, wait without repeating the cue.
breakfast.title: Breakfast

calmTime.instructions: Gentle play, a short brushing and a potty break before sleep.
calmTime.title: Quiet play, brushing and potty

farmWalk.instructions: Potty break and a calm walk in a safe part of the farm, away from the workshop and the animals.
farmWalk.title: Potty and farm exploring

fetchPlay.instructions: Toss a soft toy very close and say "fetch"; trade it for a treat with "drop it". 3–5 throws, then end calmly.
fetchPlay.title: Fetch game (retrieve)

greeting.instructions: Calm greeting and straight to the potty spot. "Good" and a treat when she's done.
greeting.title: Greeting and potty

leashWalk.instructions: Short walk on a loose leash. Reward her when she walks by your side. If she pulls, stop.
leashWalk.title: Leash walk

lunch.instructions: Midday meal. Set aside some kibble for the session treats.
lunch.title: Lunch

morningRest.instructions: A quiet spot with her chew toy. Let her sleep.
morningRest.title: Rest with a chew toy

session1.instructions: Say her name and reward her when she looks at you. Then "sit" with the treat over her head. End with something she already knows.
session1.title: Session 1: name and "sit"

session2.instructions: Crouch down 3–6 ft away, happy voice, "come" and a special treat when she arrives. End with something she already knows.
session2.title: Session 2: "come" from a short distance

session3.instructions: Review what she knows and try this week's new cue. End with something she already knows.
session3.title: Session 3: review and new cue

sniffGame.instructions: Hide 3–5 treats from her ration and say "find it". Stop while she still wants more.
sniffGame.title: Scent game (find it)

socialization.instructions: One new experience, at a distance where she stays calm. Reward calm and curiosity.
socialization.title: Today's socialization

tugPlay.instructions: Tug play. If her teeth touch skin: "ouch", pause the game for a few seconds, then start again.
tugPlay.title: Tug play (soft bite)

visit.instructions: Potty break and gentle handling of paws and ears, with a treat for each touch.
visit.title: Check-in: potty and handling

come.description: Comes to you when called. Special treat: boiled chicken.

howTo.levelUp: She comes at once 4 times out of 5: increase the distance, then call her from another room, then in the fenced yard.
howTo.mistakes: Calling her for something she dislikes (a bath, being shut in), calling when she surely will not come, and scolding her when she finally arrives.
howTo.setup: Boiled chicken in small pieces, only for this exercise. Start indoors, 1–2 yards from her and, if you can, with a second person.
howTo.step1: Crouch down, open your arms and say her name and “come” once, in a happy voice.
howTo.step2: Take one or two steps back to invite her to follow you.
howTo.step3: When she reaches you, gently hold her collar, say “good” and give her the chicken.
howTo.step4: Release her with “joga” so coming to you does not always mean the fun is over.
howTo.step5: With two people, call her in turns from different spots in the room.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she does not come, do not repeat or chase her: run the other way, crouch down or make a funny noise, and make the next call easier and closer.

come.name: Come

down.description: Lies down following the treat from nose to floor.

howTo.levelUp: She lies down at once 4 times out of 5: use a smaller gesture, then practice in other places with few distractions.
howTo.mistakes: Pushing her shoulders down, moving the treat too fast, and asking her to stay down for long at this age.
howTo.setup: She already sits well. A quiet place, a soft floor or rug and treats in your hand.
howTo.step1: Ask her to sit, hold a treat at her nose and lower it slowly straight down to the floor, between her front paws.
howTo.step2: Then slide it slowly along the floor away from her: she will stretch out and lie down.
howTo.step3: The moment her elbows touch the floor, say “good” and give her the treat on the floor.
howTo.step4: After about 5 good repetitions, add the word “down” just before the hand movement.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she stands up, move the treat more slowly and closer to her chest; reward halfway (head low) and build up little by little.

down.name: Down

leash.description: Walks next to you on a loose leash.

howTo.levelUp: 4 out of 5 short walks with a loose leash: walk longer stretches, then in the yard with more smells, then along the farm track.
howTo.mistakes: Pulling the leash back, jerking it, letting her get where she wants by pulling, and walks that are too long for her age.
howTo.setup: A light collar or harness and a 6-foot leash. Start indoors or in the yard, before a walk, with treats in the hand on her side.
howTo.step1: Let her wear the collar and leash for a few minutes while she eats or plays, so she gets used to them.
howTo.step2: Walk a few steps; every time she is next to your leg with a loose leash, say “good” and give her a treat next to your leg.
howTo.step3: If the leash goes tight, stop and stand still; as soon as it loosens, say “good” and keep walking.
howTo.step4: Change direction often and reward her when she follows you.
howTo.step5: When she walks at your side most of the time, say “heel” just as she reaches your leg, then reward.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she pulls all the time, the place is too exciting: go back somewhere quieter and reward more often, every one or two steps.

leash.name: Leash

leaveIt.description: Moves away from a closed hand or something on the ground.

howTo.levelUp: She moves away at once 4 times out of 5: uncover the treat a little, then leave it on the floor in sight, ready to cover it.
howTo.mistakes: Letting her eat the forbidden treat after leaving it, saying “leave it” over and over, and using it in situations she cannot win yet.
howTo.setup: Two kinds of treats: plain ones in a closed hand and better ones in the other hand. Sit on the floor next to her.
howTo.step1: Show her your closed hand with a treat inside and let her sniff, lick or paw at it without opening it.
howTo.step2: The moment she moves her nose away, say “good” and give her a treat from the other hand, never the one in the closed hand.
howTo.step3: Repeat until she moves away quickly; then say “leave it” just as you show the closed hand.
howTo.step4: Next, put the treat on the floor under your hand and do the same.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she manages to grab it, it was too hard: go back to the closed hand and make the next repetitions easier.

leaveIt.name: Leave it

name.description: Turns her head and looks at you when she hears her name.

howTo.levelUp: She turns at once 4 times out of 5: practice in the yard, then with a family member walking past, then from a little farther away.
howTo.mistakes: Repeating her name over and over, rewarding late, and calling her only to end something fun.
howTo.setup: A quiet room and about 10 pea-sized treats from her daily ration. Train before a meal, when she is keen.
howTo.step1: When she is not looking at you, say her name once in a happy voice.
howTo.step2: The instant she turns her head, say “good” and give the treat within a second.
howTo.step3: Wait until she looks away, then repeat. No more than 5 times per session.
howTo.step4: Never use her name to scold her or before something she dislikes: her name must always predict good things.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she does not turn, the place is too exciting or you are too far: move closer, go somewhere quieter and try again next session.

name.name: Name

potty.description: Goes potty in the usual spot.

howTo.levelUp: She goes in her spot 4 times out of 5: space the outings out a little, as long as there are no accidents.
howTo.mistakes: Scolding accidents (it teaches her to hide), rewarding late once back inside, and changing the spot.
howTo.setup: Choose one spot in the yard, always the same. Take her there when she wakes up, after eating, after playing and every 1–2 hours.
howTo.step1: Carry her or walk her on the leash straight to the spot, without playing on the way.
howTo.step2: Wait quietly; as she starts, say “go potty” in a calm voice.
howTo.step3: When she finishes, say “good” and give her a treat right there, within seconds.
howTo.step4: Then, as a bonus, a little play or exploring.
howTo.troubleshoot: If there is an accident, clean it with an enzymatic cleaner without saying anything and take her out more often; an accident only means she needed to go out sooner.

potty.name: Potty

retrieve.description: Brings a toy back to you and trades it for a treat: a game that suits her retriever nature.

howTo.levelUp: She brings it back 4 times out of 5: toss it a little farther, then in the yard, then in the grass of the farm.
howTo.mistakes: Chasing her to take the toy, pulling it out of her mouth, long sessions, and making endless ball chasing the center of her day.
howTo.setup: A soft toy she likes and treats in your pocket. A quiet room or corridor, when she is playful but not overexcited.
howTo.step1: Wiggle the toy on the floor and toss it very close, one or two yards away.
howTo.step2: When she picks it up, praise her happily and take a few steps back so she follows you with the toy.
howTo.step3: When she reaches you, show her a treat and say “drop it”; as she lets go, say “good”, give the treat and pick up the toy.
howTo.step4: Once she brings it back every time, say “fetch” just as you toss it.
howTo.step5: Stop after 3–5 throws, while she still wants more, and end calmly with a chew toy.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she runs off with the toy, do not chase her: move away from her, crouch down and call her happily, and use a shorter distance or a corridor next time.

retrieve.name: Retrieve

search.description: Finds food by smell: first in plain sight, then hidden in a room, then around the farm.

howTo.levelUp: She finds it easily 4 times out of 5: hide it in another room, then in the grass of the yard, then around the farm (weeks 2 and 3 of the plan).
howTo.mistakes: Always pointing at the food, hiding it too hard too soon, and long sessions that tire her.
howTo.setup: 5 treats or kibbles from her ration and a room with no other food in sight. Hold her gently, or ask someone to, while you place the food.
howTo.step1: Let her watch you put a treat on the floor a yard away, say “find it” and let her go to eat it.
howTo.step2: Repeat with the treat half hidden: behind a chair leg or under the corner of a cloth.
howTo.step3: Hide it out of sight in the same room, say “find it” and let her work it out with her nose; praise her calmly when she finds it.
howTo.step4: Stop after 3–5 finds, while she still wants more.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gives up or looks at you, make it easier: put the food back in sight or closer and help her by pointing near it.

search.name: Search

sit.description: Sits on the verbal cue or the hand signal.

howTo.levelUp: She sits at once 4 times out of 5: say “sit” with a smaller gesture, then in other rooms, then in the yard with few distractions.
howTo.mistakes: Pushing her rear down, saying “sit” several times, and rewarding when she is already getting up.
howTo.setup: Stand in front of her in a quiet place with treats in your hand. Do not say the word yet.
howTo.step1: Hold a treat at her nose and move it slowly up and back over her head: her rear will go down on its own.
howTo.step2: The moment her rear touches the floor, say “good” and give the treat.
howTo.step3: After about 5 good repetitions, make the same movement with an empty hand and reward from the other hand.
howTo.step4: When she always sits following your hand, say “sit” just before the gesture.
howTo.step5: Release her with “joga” so she knows the exercise is over.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she jumps, your hand is too high: keep it right at her nose. If she backs away, practice with a wall behind her.

sit.name: Sit

softBite.description: Controls the strength of her bite during play.

howTo.levelUp: She softens her mouth at once 4 times out of 5: play a little longer and have the rest of the family follow the same rule.
howTo.mistakes: Pulling your hand away fast (it invites chasing), shouting, tapping her muzzle, and only some people following the rule.
howTo.setup: Play on the floor with a rope or a soft chew toy at hand. Short games, when she is calm, not when she is overtired.
howTo.step1: Play gently with her using your hands and the toy.
howTo.step2: If her teeth press hard on your skin, say “ouch” in a soft, high voice and stop the game for a few seconds, hands still.
howTo.step3: When she calms down, offer her the toy and keep playing; say “good” if she bites the toy.
howTo.step4: If she bites hard again, end the game calmly and leave her a chew toy.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gets more excited, she is tired or overstimulated: give her a chew toy and let her rest; sleepy puppies bite more.

softBite.name: Soft bite

stay.description: Holds a sit for a few seconds until released with “joga”.

howTo.levelUp: She holds it 4 times out of 5: increase time or distance, never both at once, then add a few distractions.
howTo.mistakes: Calling her to you out of the “stay” (that is another exercise), forgetting the release word, and increasing time and distance together.
howTo.setup: She already sits every time. Stand in front of her in a quiet place with the treats ready.
howTo.step1: Ask her to sit, show her your open palm and say “stay” once.
howTo.step2: Count one second, say “good” and give her the treat while she is still sitting.
howTo.step3: Release her with “joga” and invite her to move.
howTo.step4: Add one second at a time: 2, 3, 5 seconds, always rewarding before she gets up.
howTo.step5: Later, take one small step back and return to her to reward.
howTo.troubleshoot: If she gets up before you release her, you asked too much: go back to the last time or distance she managed and build from there.

stay.name: Stay

animalAdultDogs.howTo: Only known, vaccinated, calm dogs, once your vet says it's OK.
animalAdultDogs.label: Vaccinated, well-balanced adult dogs

animalCats.howTo: On leash; the cat must be free to leave. Reward calm.
animalCats.label: Cats

animalPoultryLivestock.howTo: Always on leash and at a distance; reward her for looking and then looking back at you.
animalPoultryLivestock.label: Hens or livestock (on leash)

handlingBrushing.howTo: Two or three strokes and a treat.
handlingBrushing.label: Brushing

handlingCollar.howTo: Put it on during meals or play; take it off when she's calm.
handlingCollar.label: Collar

handlingEars.howTo: Lift an ear for a second and reward.
handlingEars.label: Ears

handlingHarness.howTo: Let her put her own head through to get a treat; buckle it and reward.
handlingHarness.label: Harness

handlingMouth.howTo: Lift her lip for a second and reward.
handlingMouth.label: Mouth

handlingNails.howTo: Show her the nail clipper and touch her nails with it, without cutting; treat.
handlingNails.label: Nails

handlingPaws.howTo: Touch a paw for a second and reward; build up slowly.
handlingPaws.label: Paws

handlingTail.howTo: Touch her tail gently and reward.
handlingTail.label: Tail

noiseAngleGrinder.howTo: From outside the workshop and far away; short bursts with treats.
noiseAngleGrinder.label: Angle grinder

noiseBrushcutter.howTo: Far away and briefly; reward calm.
noiseBrushcutter.label: Brush cutter

noiseCar.howTo: Engine running at a distance; move closer bit by bit if she stays calm.
noiseCar.label: Car

noiseChainsaw.howTo: Far away and briefly; reward calm.
noiseChainsaw.label: Chainsaw

noiseHammer.howTo: Single blows at a distance; a treat after each one.
noiseHammer.label: Hammer

noiseThunderFireworks.howTo: A recording at very low volume during meals; turn it up a little on different days.
noiseThunderFireworks.label: Thunder or fireworks (recording)

noiseTractor.howTo: Start far away, with treats while it runs. Never bring her closer if she gets scared.
noiseTractor.label: Tractor

noiseWelder.howTo: Noise at a distance, without looking at the arc; short bursts with treats.
noiseWelder.label: Welder

peopleCap.howTo: Put the cap on in front of her and reward while she watches.
peopleCap.label: People wearing caps

peopleChildren.howTo: Children sitting calmly, with an adult nearby; one treat each.
peopleChildren.label: Children

peopleGlasses.howTo: Sunglasses and safety glasses; reward calm.
peopleGlasses.label: People wearing glasses

peopleHelmet.howTo: First leave the helmet on the ground so she can sniff it; then put it on.
peopleHelmet.label: People wearing helmets

peopleMen.howTo: Have him crouch down and offer a treat with an open hand.
peopleMen.label: Men

peopleVisitors.howTo: Have the visitor ignore her on arrival and reward her when she comes over on her own.
peopleVisitors.label: Visitors

peopleWomen.howTo: Have her crouch down and offer a treat with an open hand.
peopleWomen.label: Women

peopleWorkwear.howTo: Coveralls, boots and gloves; let her sniff them first.
peopleWorkwear.label: Work clothes

placeCar.howTo: First inside the parked car, with treats; then very short rides.
placeCar.label: Car

placeGrass.howTo: Short grass; play and a treat.
placeGrass.label: Grass

placeGravel.howTo: Let her explore at her own pace and reward every step.
placeGravel.label: Gravel

placeMetal.howTo: A metal sheet on the ground, held firmly so it doesn't rattle; reward every step.
placeMetal.label: Metal

placeMud.howTo: A small mud puddle; reward her when she steps in it.
placeMud.label: Mud

placeShallowWater.howTo: Water below her paws, on a mild day; never force her.
placeShallowWater.label: Shallow water

placeStairs.howTo: Just one or two steps, going up; help her down.
placeStairs.label: Stairs

placeVetSocialVisit.howTo: Go in, get treats and leave, with no exam.
placeVetSocialVisit.label: Social visit to the vet
